title: What is proven, what is not, what comes next
blurb: An honest ledger as of Oct 9: which parts have a result, which are only built or planned, the open risks, and what comes next.

scenes.heading: Result one: the thinking does the work
caption: Result one. On 6,040 questions kept aside, the model scored 73.01 out of 100 with its thinking on.
With thinking switched off it scored 0.66. A plain model of the same size scored 67.12.
So the thinking does the work, on one copy at the smallest size. Bigger sizes are untested.

scenes.heading: Result two: the calculator can sit outside

caption.text: Result two. The calculator is plain code outside the model. In the tested version the thinker writes a slip; the reader reads the reply.
Over 6 copies it scored 0.62 points above a similar calculator-inside design. The likely range includes zero.
With the calculator switched off, the questions that need it score 0.0, so the model really uses it.

scenes.heading: The next gates, in order

caption.text: In order: the size test finishes, then a test of experts (many small specialist networks, not covered here).
Then a 100M fit check (memory and speed) and the four pieces together at 3M.
Then hand-written pieces are replaced, 10M and 30M follow, and a results readout is planned for Oct 31.
One big run waits for clear results and for the plan to be 90% sure it passes its marks.

scenes.heading: What to remember
caption: The thinking does the work, shown on one copy at the smallest size.
The calculator can sit outside, shown on 6 copies at 3M, with two checks not clean. Most of the rest is built or planned.
The plan's judgment: nothing is ready to buy. It works at 3M, but nobody has shown it improves faster with size than a plain model.
